archetype.name: Bubble Team (power-play driven)
archetype.definition: A club that can stay near the Pacific's playoff line on special teams and hot finishing while getting out-chanced at 5-on-5, so its spot depends on how long the power play and shooting keep covering for that.

report.headline: A power play and hot sticks are hiding a team still being out-chanced.
report.take:
Anaheim comes into the week on a three-game skid, and the early numbers look like last season's team with a different cover. The Ducks made a real jump in 2025-26, finishing 43-33-6 with 92 points and six playoff wins. They did it while being outscored, with a -0.18 Goal Diff / GP propped up by a +4.2 Pts vs Goal Diff. The 2024-25 group leaned on the same kind of close-game luck at +3.7. This year's start is no different at heart. The record is roughly .500, the differential is -2, and the 82-game pace reads 94 points with a -20 goal differential. That is a bubble team's profile, not a riser's.

The power play is doing the lifting. At 26.9% it ranks 6th, well above the league's 20.4%. Leo Carlsson has 7 of his 9 points with the man advantage, and Beckett Sennecke has turned 18 shots into 5 goals. Overall finishing is running at 13.0%, 8th in the league and well above the 11.3% average. On a team that ranks 27th with 24.1 shots a game, that rate is the only reason the offense sits mid-pack at 3.0 goals a game.

The 5-on-5 picture is where the record is flattered. Anaheim allows only 21.7 shots a game, 3rd fewest, which looks like a stingy defense. But its xGF % of 47.8% ranks 24th. The few shots it allows are dangerous ones, and the goalies are not the problem. Team save % is .882, 21st, yet Goalies GSAx is +2.4, and Lukas Dostal sits at +0.7 despite a 3.17 GAA. Average goaltending would have allowed more on these chances. The blueline grades D+, and Jackson LaCombe is losing his minutes badly at a 40.8% xGF share in 26.55 a night.

The direction is mildly worrying: the last five games are 2-3-0 with a .400 points percentage. The schedule now offers a cushion, with two of the league's worst three teams on the slate. The question is whether the Ducks can start generating chances at even strength before the shooting cools. Until the 5-on-5 share moves toward 50%, this is a team that will hover around the cut line rather than climb above it.

strengths.title: A top-six power play
strengths.body: The man advantage is converting at 26.9%, 6th in the league and well above the league average. Carlsson is the hub, with 7 power-play points, and Granlund, Sennecke and Gauthier all contribute. Last season's unit finished at 18.6%, so some cooling is likely, but there is real skill here. It should stay above average.

strengths.title: Goaltending saving above expectation
strengths.body: The .882 team save % looks ugly, but the goalies have saved 2.4 goals more than expected on the chances they've faced. The quality of shots against is the issue, not the netminding. Ville Husso has been sharp in limited work at +1.5. A B- goaltending grade is a floor this team can count on.

strengths.title: Low shot volume against
strengths.body: Opponents are getting only 21.7 shots a game, 3rd fewest in the league. That keeps games tight and limits the damage when the defense breaks down. Because the chances that do get through are high quality, though, it is more a containment style than true defensive control.

concerns.title: Out-chanced at even strength
concerns.body: An xGF % of 47.8% ranks 24th, and the Ducks rank 27th in shots for. They aren't driving play, and the low shots-against count masks how dangerous the looks they give up are. Last year's xGF % was 51.9%, so this is a step back rather than a known baseline. It is the number most likely to decide their season.

concerns.title: Finishing running above sustainable
concerns.body: A 13.0% shooting rate on few shots is propping up a league-average offense. Sennecke is scoring on more than a quarter of his shots. When the percentage drifts toward the league's 11.3%, the scoring will dip unless shot volume rises.

concerns.title: A thin, overmatched blueline
concerns.body: The defense grades D+, and the No. 1 minutes go to LaCombe, whose 40.8% xGF share is among the worst on the roster. Travis Mitchell ranks 235th of 242 on his tab. The group has one goal among its six listed defensemen. It neither suppresses quality chances nor helps tilt the ice.

trend.note: A 4-1 start through Calgary has turned into three straight losses, each by two or more goals. The last five games carry a .400 points percentage, below the season rate.

weekAhead.headline: Eastern road swing ends against the league's worst team
weekAhead.body:
Three road games in four nights out East, then Vancouver at home. The Islanders are the hardest test. They rank 3rd in goals against on the back of an A-grade goalie group: a .940 save % and a league-best +10.4 GSAx. Anaheim's high-percentage finishing runs straight into that wall. New Jersey is the opposite kind of opponent. The Devils lead the league in xGF % and fire 35 shots a game, which will test Anaheim's shot suppression. But their goaltending grades D- and their PK sits at 69.6%, a clean opening for the Ducks' power play.

The back half is soft. Philadelphia is 1-6-3, last in xGF % and in shooting, and allows 32.8 shots a game. Vancouver ranks 32nd on the site, kills just 58.1% of penalties and gives up points freely to every position. Anything less than a winning week would be a red flag; three or more wins is the realistic bar.

keyMatchups.title: Ducks power play vs. weak kills
keyMatchups.body: New Jersey's 69.6% PK ranks 27th and Vancouver's 58.1% is last. Anaheim's top-six power play is its best weapon. This is the week for Carlsson and company to pile up points and paper over the 5-on-5 deficit.

keyMatchups.title: Finishing vs. Islanders' goaltending
keyMatchups.body: New York's goalies lead the league in GSAx and hold opponents' centers furthest under expectation outside one team. On low shot volume, Anaheim needs its finishing to hold up. Against this netminding it probably won't, so a low-scoring night is likely.

keyMatchups.title: Devils' volume against Ducks' structure
keyMatchups.body: New Jersey leads the league in shots a game and shot-attempt share, while Anaheim allows the 3rd-fewest shots. If the Devils pin the Ducks in their zone, the D+ blueline gets exposed. Dostal would then need his best game of the young season.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Anaheim out-chances Philadelphia and Vancouver at 5-on-5. If it can't tilt the ice against the two worst possession teams in the league, the xGF problem is structural.

restOfSeason.body:
The power play and goaltending give Anaheim a floor, and last season's 92 points show the core can hang around the race. But the start rests on finishing that should cool. The team is not getting its usual bounce in close games either, with Pts vs Goal Diff near zero after two straight years well above it. Without that luck, a below-50% chance share points to a slightly negative goal differential and a points total a bit under last year's. The 94-point pace looks generous.

The upside path is the 5-on-5 share returning toward last season's 51.9% while the power play stays in the top ten. That would make the Ducks a legitimate wild-card contender. If LaCombe's pairing keeps bleeding chances and the shooting regresses, expect something in the mid-80s and a spot on the outside looking in. I'd project 84 to 94 points, with the power play settling in the low 20s.
